name: Evanston Plan Commission
dek: The Tuesday-night room where the city’s next shape is argued in public.
summary: A nine-member citizen commission that reviews zoning, planned developments, and the stories a city tells itself about density. Fountain Square and Main Street Lofts are both on the docket.

name: Maya Chen
dek: City planning director — the staff voice in the Tuesday room.
summary: Planning director for the City of Evanston (demo portrait). Chen’s memos on Fountain Square and Maple Avenue have become the unofficial syllabus for anyone trying to follow downtown.

name: Elias Ward
dek: Architect of the Fountain Square proposal now in review.
summary: Principal of a Chicago studio asked to make a quieter tower and a wetter plaza. Ward’s drawings put the fountain back on axis with Church Street — a move that has already divided the room.

name: Rosa Delgado
dek: Chair of the Downtown Partnership; keeper of Saturday.
summary: A Central Street retailer who now chairs the downtown business partnership (demo portrait). Delgado’s test for any Fountain Square plan is simple: does the farmers market still fit?

name: Nate Okonkwo
dek: The alderman who keeps asking who the plaza is for.
summary: A ward alderman (demo portrait) whose questions at Plan Commission tend to be about ground-floor life rather than height. He has become the unofficial narrator of the Fountain Square file.
